title: Typed multi-channel prefetch SDK playbook (PRD)
content:
Goal and context:

This is a working PRD/playbook for an SDK-first approach to multi-channel, typed prefetching for Hosted API streaming + tool-calling workflows. The goal is to provide a small set of well-documented SDK primitives that let clients request, observe, and reconcile partial results coming from multiple channels (LLM stream, tool responses, attachments, metadata), while still preserving predictable latency SLOs and easy migration paths for existing sync/stream users.

Why this matters:
- Customers build complex UIs that interleave conversational text with tool outputs (search snippets, code execution results, 3rd-party API payloads).
- Naive streaming exposes race conditions: UI jitter, reordering, duplicated updates, and poor retry semantics.
- We can reduce network round trips and wasted tokens by prefetching toollets and structured objects where it makes sense, and by exposing typed contracts to SDKs for safer client reconciliation.

Non-goals:
- Replacing server-side orchestration logic for enterprise workflows (this is SDK/playbook not runtime replacement).
- Covering 30+ edge-case tool graphs in v1; focus on common patterns (single tool, tool fanout with bounded parallelism, attachment download).

Key concepts (short definitions):
- Channel: independent stream of semantic updates (e.g., "model-text", "tool:search", "attachment:thumbnail").
- Typed fragment: a structured, schema-backed partial result belonging to a named channel (JSON schema pointer or lightweight type token).
- Prefetch hint: client-provided or server-suggested instruction to fetch resources (examples: prewarm tools, resolve attachments, run narrow rerank).
- Commitment frame: an incremental commit that marks a fragment as durable for the UI (idempotent).

User scenarios (prioritized):
1) Autocomplete with inline citation cards: model streams summary; prefetch search top-3 in parallel with low-cost reranker; occasional attachment fetch for image preview.
2) Code assistant that runs linters/test in a sandbox: LLM suggests patch; SDK prefetches execution to provide immediate "can-run" preview then final results.
3) Customer-support agent: streaming transcript + immediate tooling to fetch related tickets; client needs to show partial ticket fields as soon as available.

API primitives (SDK surface):
- openSession(opts) -> session handle with defaults (channels allowed, max-prefetch-parallelism, backpressure-policy).
- requestResponse(session, prompt, {channels: ["model-text","tool:search"], prefetch: [{channel:"tool:search", mode:"top-k", k:3}]}) -> returns stream handle.
- onFragment(stream, callback(fragment)) -> receives typed fragments: {channel, type, content, sequence, committed}.
- commitFragment(stream, fragmentId) -> idempotent commit (for UX to mark stable state).
- snapshot(stream) -> returns last-known committed state for reconciliation (useful for reconnect).
- abortChannel(stream, channelName, reason) -> signal to server to halt background prefetches.

Ergonomics & developer patterns:
- Default to optimistic lightweight prefetch: prefetch low-cost tool results (cacheable search, quick probes) when token budget permits; require explicit opt-in for expensive runs (compute-heavy sandboxes).
- Typing: expose typed TypeScript interfaces and JSON-schema URLs for each declared channel. SDK should validate fragments locally (lenient mode for forward-compat).
- Backpressure: two-lever model: client-visible pacing (UI update frequency) + server throttles for expensive channels. SDK exposes a simple setPrefetchBudget() API.
- Low-bandwidth mobile: allow partial hydration where attachments are deferred and replaced with placeholders until user taps.

Protocol notes (server + SDK):
- Multi-channel multiplexing over a single streaming socket (websocket/HTTP2) with lightweight frame headers: {channel, seq, frag-id, type-hint, committed-flag}.
- Prefetch hints attached to requests, plus server-suggested prefetch proposals in early frames.
- Fallbacks: when socket connectivity is unreliable, SDK should switch to a REST fallback for non-streaming commit/snapshot operations and mark UI accordingly.

Observability & SLOs:
- Telemetry: per-channel latency histograms (time to first fragment, time to committed), prefetch success rate, budget spent per-request, abort/retry counts.
- SLO proposals: 95th percentile time-to-first-model-fragment < 120ms (hosted fast-path), median tool-prefetch < 300ms for cached/text tools.

Migration plan from existing Streaming SDK:
1) Provide compatibility wrapper that maps current stream events into channel "model-text" fragments with minimal client changes.
2) Add opt-in API flags enabling prefetch hints and typed fragments.
3) Ship telemetry and sample SDK adapters; run beta with 5 customers.

Security and safety considerations:
- Tool prefetches must follow tenant isolation and data-scoping rules. Prefetch hints cannot escalate privileges; server validates per-tenant policies.
- Attachments: signed, expiring URLs; SDK must validate content-type before rendering.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Schema discovery: host JSON schemas under a stable CDN or embed type tokens with backward-compatibility rules? (impact: runtime validation overhead).
- Prefetch budgeting: server-controlled quota per-API-key vs. client-declared soft-budgets.
- Commitment semantics for multi-fragment transactions across channels (do we need multi-fragment commit atomicity?).

Short-term milestones (next 10 weeks):
- Week 1: internal design review + protocol sketch (proto frames, type-hint layout).
- Weeks 2–4: TypeScript SDK prototype: openSession, requestResponse, onFragment, commitFragment; local validation harness.
- Weeks 5–7: Server prototype: channel multiplexing + simple prefetch engine (search tool stub, attachment stub).
- Weeks 8–10: Beta with 3 partners; collect telemetry; iterate on default budgets and schema layout.

Action items (owners):
- Asha: finalize protocol sketch and confluence page by 2025-02-17.
- Kai: TypeScript SDK prototype + tests by 2025-03-03.
- Marina: infra prototype for channel multiplexing and prefetch scheduler by 2025-03-10.

Notes to reviewers (quick read):
- Focus review on SDK ergonomics (are the primitives small and composable?), and on the prefetch defaulting policy (we want a conservative default to avoid surprise cost spikes).
- If you have production examples where prefetching made UX worse (or costly), add them inline below — we will use them to refine prefetch heuristics.

Rough appendix ideas (to be filled):
- Example client code snippets (TS) for the 3 scenarios above.
- Wire-format examples and a tiny reference implementation (python websocket client).
- Cost model worked example comparing with/without prefetch for a 50 req/min app.

-- end of draft (notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight; want a tangible SDK shim that teams can reason about and iterate against)
